subject: Private/on-prem follow-up: air-gapped ops, upgrades & hardware constraints
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>

Subject: Private/on-prem follow-up: air-gapped ops, upgrades & hardware constraints

Gina — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our side and a handful of follow-up questions so we can size the on-prem plan and prepare a runbook for BiomedCorp's air-gapped environment.

Recap (what we heard)
- You want a fully private deployment inside your datacenter with no outbound internet except an approved jump host.
- Hardware will be procured by BiomedCorp (you asked for Redwood recommendations).
- Upgrade windows will be tightly controlled; on-site approver required for any firmware or kernel changes.
- Acceptance test: smoke model run + 5 QPS sustained, basic latency targets.

Open questions / asks for next steps
1) Hardware limits: can you confirm target node counts and GPU models you are considering (serial/model preferred). If you don’t have final SKUs I attached an "onprem-hw-checklist.pdf" with recommended minimums and optional high-performance options.
2) Maintenance window: is your preferred weekly window Sunday 02:00–06:00 UTC (you mentioned weekends) or do you have a different fixed window for maintenance?
3) Outbound connectivity: you said only an approved jump host is allowed — can you share the jump host IP(s) and whether it supports mutual TLS or jump-host bastion auth?
4) Automated updates: to align with air-gapped policy, do you require that Redwood provide an offline installer and manual upgrade process (no automatic background updates)?
5) KMS/HSM: confirm whether you have an HSM (model/vendor) we should integrate with for disk and artifact signing.
6) On-call escalation: provide the on-site engineer contact and our PO/procurement contact so we can draft the SOW and support SLAs.

Attachments in this message: redwood-onprem-hw-checklist.pdf, rdw-sow-draft.docx, biomed-acceptance-tests.xlsx

Next steps proposed by us
- Technical deep-dive workshop (90 minutes) next week with your infra and security teams so Soojin and Marissa can capture runbook constraints.
- After workshop, Redwood will prepare an offline installer bundle, signed artifacts, and a proposed rollback plan for upgrades.
- Draft SOW + procurement checklist for your Purchasing team.

Please reply with the hardware/maintenance answers above and a couple of time slots for the workshop. Thanks — happy to coordinate.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private/on-prem follow-up: air-gapped ops, upgrades & hardware constraints

Diego — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers inline, then a couple of constraints from our side:

1) Hardware: we are evaluating two options: 2x 2U servers with 4x H100 (preferred) or 3x 1U nodes with 2x A100 80GB. We expect to start with 2 racks. I’ll share exact SKUs by Wednesday.
2) Maintenance window: Sunday 02:00–06:00 UTC works for us for planned maintenance.
3) Outbound connectivity: only one jump host is allowed (10.0.0.45 on our private mgmt VLAN). It supports mutual TLS with client certs. No other outbound ports permitted.
4) Automated updates: we cannot allow automatic updates. Offline installer with signed packages is required.
5) KMS/HSM: we have an HSM (Thales Luna 7) for key wrapping — integration required.
6) On-call escalation: point person is Andrew Li (andrew.li@biomedcorp.com). Purchasing is included here; our PO process takes ~10 business days once SOW is final.

Acceptance tests: we want a smoke test using our s2i dataset and then a 24-hour soak at 5 QPS. If that passes, we proceed to certification. I attached the acceptance matrix (biomed-acceptance-tests.xlsx).

Two constraints:
- Firmware and kernel changes require an explicit on-site signoff from our datacenter manager.
- Any remote debug that requires outbound access must be routed through the jump host and approved by our security team in advance.

We can do the workshop next Thursday (Dec 3) 15:00–16:30 UTC or Friday (Dec 4) 09:00–10:30 UTC. Which works for your team?

Thanks,
Gina
Senior Infrastructure Manager
BiomedCorp

Subject: Re: Private/on-prem follow-up: air-gapped ops, upgrades & hardware constraints

Gina — appreciate the detail. Technical clarifications and what Redwood will provide for an air-gapped/offline deployment: 

High-level offline support model
- Offline installer bundle: an immutable tarball containing signed container images and a verified install script. Delivered via secure transfer (S3 presigned -> your secure download or encrypted USB courier).
- Signed PKI artifacts: we will provide signed image digests and a verification tool that runs locally against the bundle.
- Upgrade flow: manual-trigger upgrades only. Operator runs verification locally, performs a snapshot of model KV cache, installs the new images, runs smoke tests, and then switches traffic. We will provide a rollback tarball for any failed upgrade.
- Remote troubleshooting: allowed through the jump host only. Redwood engineers will request temporary session tokens and mTLS certs from you; audits are logged locally and a copy of session logs can be exchanged by SFTP.

Hardware and ops notes
- Recommended minimum config (for the options Gina described):
  * H100 option: 2 racks with 2x H100 80GB per server, NVMe mirrored boot, 512GB RAM per host, redundant PSUs.
  * A100 option: 3x nodes with 4x A100 80GB across 2 racks.
- We support offline firmware and kernel constraints: we will not push firmware updates. If you want Redwood to coordinate a firmware maintenance window, we will supply step-by-step MOP and test checklist but the on-site team must apply the firmware.
- KV cache snapshotting: we provide a snapshot/restore utility; recommend nightly snapshots before any upgrade.

Acceptance test checklist (we’ll expand during the workshop)
- Pull signed images from the offline bundle and verify signatures.
- Smoke model run (latency and correctness) + 24h soak at 5 QPS.
- Checkpoint and restore KV cache across a controlled restart.

Next items we need from BiomedCorp
1) Final SKUs or serials for procurement -> we’ll validate thermal/PSU compatibility.
2) Jump host fingerprint and permitted authentication method for mTLS.
3) Contact for datacenter manager to coordinate firmware/kernel signoffs.

I attached a short runbook template to the message we’ll use to craft the final SOW. We can use Dec 3 (15:00 UTC) for the workshop — Diego / Marissa will join.

— Soojin
Sooj in Lee
Senior Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
